title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: As transcribed, (36) reads Tr(xi rho) = 0. The derivation (and the next line, 'par (36)' giving -lambda0 Tr rho) requires Tr(xi rho) = Tr rho, as in (35). This is either a slip or a misreading.

The third relation of (36) is written with struck-through pieces. The correct form is Tr((xi eps1(1-mu) - 1) sigma) = 0, i.e. Tr(eta sigma) = Tr sigma. The page's form with '-1' inside the trace is consistent with this once interpreted correctly.
Minor: the margin note says lambda (rather than lambda0) is a central section; this is notational only.

ideas.what: Elimination of eta reduces the system to one in xi alone, and the trace condition becomes affine in mu because eps1(t) = 1 + tN is unipotent.
ideas.modern_name: elementary linear algebra / solving an affine equation over a ring

ideas.what: Hypothesis eps1 = -lambda0 rho sigma^{-1} with lambda0 = ±1. This makes the constant term Q independent of xi, so that mu = c/P(xi) with c = lambda0 Tr rho + Tr sigma a unit.
ideas.modern_name: SL2(Z) relation: the unipotent generator as a product of order-6 and order-4 elements (T = rho sigma type relation)
ideas.where_published: Possibly related material in La Longue Marche (1981); unsure

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine linear-algebraic manipulation within a larger unpublished study of a GL2 'loop equation'. The page itself contains no new idea beyond solving an affine equation for mu.
transcription_corrections: (36) second relation should read Tr(xi rho) = Tr rho (as required by the later use 'par (36)'), not '= 0'.
Third relation of (36) and (38): read Tr((xi eps1(1-mu) - 1) sigma) = 0. The 'overline sigma_xi' is an artefact for sigma.
'en divisant par mu' is doubtful. Likely 'qui est affine par rapport à mu et par rapport aux coefficients de xi'.
